papers.title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU

summary.tldr: ABot-World-0 is an action-conditioned video world model enabling real-time, long-horizon interactive world rollout on a single desktop GPU, utilizing multi-source data and distillation techniques.
key_points: Utilizes a multi-source data infrastructure from AAA games, simulation engines, and internet videos, with agent-driven collection and 14 deterministic quality checks.
Employs progressive distillation from a bidirectional action-conditioned teacher to a causal student via teacher forcing and ODE distillation, introducing LongForcing to align long self-rollouts.
Achieves 720P video streaming at up to 16 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU with 1.2s action-to-first-frame latency and 19GiB peak VRAM, through a co-designed streaming inference stack.
Integrates raw keyboard actions for unified control and reference-character memory for persistent appearance cues during third-person rollouts.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables high-fidelity, interactive virtual world generation and exploration on consumer-grade hardware, expanding accessibility for research and development.

papers.title: DataFlow-Harness: A Grounded Code-Agent Platform for Constructing Editable LLM Data Pipelines

summary.tldr: DataFlow-Harness is a platform guiding LLM agents to construct platform-native DAGs via typed, incremental mutations, bridging the NL2Pipeline gap for editable data pipelines.
key_points: DataFlow-Harness uses DataFlow-Skills for procedural guidance, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) for live operator registry and pipeline state, and DataFlow-WebUI for conversational authoring and visual DAG editing.
Achieved a 93.3% observed end-to-end pass rate on a 12-task data-engineering benchmark.
Reduced monetary cost by 72.5% and generation latency by 49.9% compared to Vanilla Claude Code.
Its observed pass rate is within 0.9 percentage points of Context-Aware Claude Code, with 42.8% lower cost.
Skills are most effective when construction requires implicit procedural knowledge.
summary.why_it_matters: This platform enables the creation of persistent, editable workflow artifacts with high reliability and reduced construction costs and latency.

papers.title: Generative World Renderer at the Speed of Play

summary.tldr: AlayaRenderer-Flash achieves real-time generative world rendering at 31.54 FPS by reformulating AlayaRenderer as an autoregressive streaming model with distilled codecs, enabling interactive world modeling.
key_points: AlayaRenderer-Flash reformulates the original AlayaRenderer into a few-step autoregressive streaming model.
It incorporates lightweight distilled codecs for efficient latent encoding and frame reconstruction.
The model increases rendering speed from 0.56 FPS (AlayaRenderer) to 31.54 FPS.
AlayaRenderer-Flash maintains the G-buffer and text-prompt interfaces of the teacher model.
It enables continuous rendering over input streams of unbounded length.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement allows for fully playable generative worlds running at 30 FPS, integrating directly with physics engines for interactive experiences.

papers.title: Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing

summary.tldr: Mage-Flow introduces a 4B-scale generative stack for efficient text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing, using a lightweight VAE and rectified flow matching for improved throughput and performance.
key_points: Mage-Flow is a 4B-scale generative stack comprising Mage-VAE and a Native-Resolution Multimodal Diffusion Transformer trained with rectified flow matching.
Mage-VAE uses one-step diffusion-style encoding/decoding with anchor-latent regularization, reducing tokenization cost by over an order of magnitude while preserving reconstruction quality.
The stack achieves 2.5x end-to-end training throughput improvement through native-resolution packing and stack-level CUDA kernel fusion.
Mage-Flow-Turbo generates a 1024^2 image in 0.59s and Mage-Flow-Edit-Turbo edits in 1.02s on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables practical, interactive high-resolution image generation and editing with a compact model, making advanced capabilities more accessible.

papers.title: Text Template Tokens Are Implicit Semantic Registers in Diffusion Transformers

summary.tldr: A causal interpretability framework for DiTs reveals structural template tokens act as implicit semantic registers, acquiring object identity from image latents rather than directly from prompt tokens.
key_points: Structural template tokens, despite lacking prompt-specific information at the encoder output, become dominant image-to-text attention sinks and causally maintain object identity within DiTs.
Prompt semantics are first injected into image latents and then read back into template tokens, rather than direct transfer from prompt tokens.
A training-free pruning rule removes heads strongly attending to prompt tokens, reducing attention FLOPs by 20% with a 1.4-point GenEval drop.
Generative computation in DiTs is organized across heads and depth, separating semantic routing from visual synthesis, progressing from identity formation to propagation and refinement.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding DiT internal mechanisms enables more efficient model design and pruning strategies, improving performance and reducing computational cost.

papers.title: AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling -- Full Technical Report

summary.tldr: AlayaWorld is a 15B video diffusion transformer generating 24-fps 540p/720p interactive video worlds with persistent spatiotemporal consistency and efficient long-horizon generation.
key_points: AlayaWorld generates 24-fps video at 540p and 720p using a 15B video diffusion transformer.
It employs a bounded visual context combining a persistent sink frame, compressed temporal history, geometry-aligned spatial memory, and recent-frame conditioning.
Long-term drift is reduced by training with corrupted histories and prediction residuals from its own roll-outs.
A discrete autoregressive distillation formulation, combining distribution-matching, self-forcing++, and consistency distillation, reduces inference from ~30 to 4 sampling steps per chunk.
summary.why_it_matters: This model enables instant creation of customized, explorable, and continuously evolving virtual worlds from text, images, or video, bypassing labor-intensive conventional game development.

papers.title: Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) implicitly encode denoising progress as a latent representation within their residual streams, which can be extracted and manipulated to predictably alter model behavior.
key_points: DLMs encode a latent representation related to the diffusion timestep in their residual streams.
This latent signal is decodable from internal activations across layers using probes.
Steering the model along a low-dimensional subspace associated with the inferred timestep modulates denoising progress.
Modulating the inferred timestep leads to predictable changes in model confidence and entropy.
The identified representation exhibits structured and interpretable properties in activation space.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and manipulating this latent timestep representation could enable finer control over DLM generation and improve their reliability.

papers.title: Stale but Stable: Staleness-Adaptive Trust Regions for Stabilizing Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: The Staleness-Adaptive Trust Region (SAT) method stabilizes asynchronous reinforcement learning by adapting PPO clipping intervals based on staleness, using detached sampled log-ratios as a proxy.
key_points: SAT uses the detached sampled log-ratio as a practical staleness proxy.
SAT identifies high-mismatch tails within each batch via staleness-based kernel scaling.
SAT contracts only the sign-selected endpoint of the nominal PPO interval, preserving baseline behavior on ordinary tokens while enforcing conservative updates on outward bands.
SAT-GSPO w/ R3 achieved 35.83 AIME24 avg@8 at lag 1 and 34.79 at lag 8, outperforming SAT-GSPO's 34.17 at lag 1, in a decoupled asynchronous RL setup using Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, SGLang, and Megatron.
The method proves local interval containment and pointwise pessimism relative to PPO, reshaping update geometry under heterogeneous staleness.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach effectively stabilizes asynchronous reinforcement learning by addressing the challenges of staleness and policy-lag in trust-region methods.

papers.title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AgentDebugX is an open-source framework for LLM agent debugging, offering a closed-loop Detect, Attribute, Recover, Rerun workflow with multi-turn root-cause diagnosis and improved failure recovery.
key_points: DeepDebug, at AgentDebugX's core, performs multi-turn root-cause diagnosis via global trajectory understanding, structure-guided investigation, and cross-examination.
On the Who and When benchmark, DeepDebug achieved 28.8% exact agent-and-step attribution accuracy on qwen3.5-9b, outperforming single-pass baselines (21.7%).
On GAIA, DeepDebug repaired 13 of 73 failed tasks in a single rerun, increasing overall accuracy from 55.8% to 63.6%, compared to 4-6 repairs for decoupled self-correction baselines.
AgentDebugX provides a Python library, CLI, web console, installable agentic skill, and an opt-in Error Hub for sharing and reusing failure-diagnosis-repair bundles.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a structured and effective method for identifying and correcting failures in LLM agents, enhancing their reliability and performance.

papers.title: SciForma: Structure-Faithful Generation of Scientific Diagrams

summary.tldr: SciForma is a framework for structure-faithful scientific diagram generation, using a decomposed quality assessment, structured training data, and a novel optimization method to achieve high structural fidelity.
key_points: SciForma decomposes diagram quality into Component, Arrow, and Text structural axes, guided by a structural inventory.
SciFormaData-700K and SciFormaBench-2K were curated for structured training and logic-verified evaluation, respectively.
Multi-Dimensional Conjunctive Preference Optimization (M-DPO) enforces simultaneous correctness across all structural axes and adaptively routes gradients during post-training.
The structural inventory enables iterative editing at inference time to correct residual errors.
SciForma-9B surpasses open-source baselines and GPT-Image-1.5 on SciFormaBench-2K and AIBench.
summary.why_it_matters: This development enables the generation of accurate scientific methodology diagrams, crucial for clear communication of research logic, by addressing the limitations of existing models in structural fidelity.

papers.title: HPD-Parsing: Hierarchical Parallel Document Parsing

summary.tldr: HPD-Parsing introduces Hierarchical Parallel Decoding for document parsing, replacing full-page autoregressive generation with parallel block-level content decoding and progressive multi-token prediction.
key_points: HPD-Parsing utilizes a main layout branch for overall document structure and dynamically assigns block-level content decoding to concurrent branches.
Progressive multi-token prediction (P-MTP) is integrated to further reduce decoding steps within each branch.
HPD-Parsing achieves 4,752 tokens per second, demonstrating 2.62x throughput improvement over the fastest existing model and 3.06x over vanilla autoregressive baselines.
The method maintains competitive parsing accuracy while significantly increasing decoding speed.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a substantial improvement in the efficiency of unified document parsing, enabling faster processing of long documents.

papers.title: AutoIndex: Learning Representation Programs for Retrieval

summary.tldr: AutoIndex learns executable representation programs to transform raw documents for retrieval systems, optimizing document indexing rather than retriever tuning.
key_points: AutoIndex searches over programs that slice, enrich, normalize, reweight, or reorganize documents before indexing.
The framework uses validation-guided program search, where agents diagnose failures and synthesize updates, retaining only improvements to retrieval quality.
Evaluated on the CRUMB benchmark with BM25 fixed, AutoIndex improved recall over a static full-document BM25 baseline on all 8 tasks.
Average gains were +8.4% in Recall@100 and +8.3% in nDCG@10, with largest gains of +30.5% in Recall@100 and +43.6% in nDCG@10.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing document representation as an explicit target before retrieval can significantly enhance retrieval system performance.

papers.title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness

summary.tldr: A new two-level meta-rubric framework and benchmark, GAMUT, is introduced to evaluate factual completeness in long-form open-ended generation, addressing limitations of precision-focused factuality metrics.
key_points: GAMUT employs a two-level rubric representation: a structured meta-rubric for content organization and importance, compiled into a flat checklist of binary, machine-gradable rubrics scored by an LLM judge.
The benchmark includes 1,813 questions grounded in real wearable imagery across 10 domains, with evidence-backed rubrics verified by expert human annotators.
A text-only variant of the framework is also released, demonstrating its modality-agnostic nature.
Evaluation of 14 frontier and open-weight models shows the benchmark is challenging (best score 58.7% from Gemini 3.1 Pro), highly discriminative, and robust to judge choice.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables comprehensive assessment of AI-generated content by measuring factual completeness, a critical aspect often overlooked by precision-focused evaluation methods.

papers.title: Masked Visual Actions for Unified World Modeling

summary.tldr: Masked Visual Actions introduce a pixel-space control interface for video models, enabling unified world modeling by expressing actions as partially revealed visual trajectories for robotic manipulation.
key_points: Masked Visual Actions (MVA) represent actions as partially revealed trajectories of an arbitrary entity in a video, aligning with visual space priors.
Revealing robot motion allows the model to act as a forward dynamics model, predicting scene response to low-level robot actions.
Revealing desired object motion enables the model to recover robot behavior consistent with the desired outcome (inverse modeling).
A single model checkpoint, finetuned with 15 hours of masked examples from real videos and simulation, achieves strong visual fidelity and controllability.
MVA supports imagined rollouts for policy evaluation, ranking candidate futures in model-based planning, and synthesizing robot motion from desired object motion.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach improves robotic manipulation by providing a unified visual interface for forward dynamics, inverse modeling, and planning, enhancing decision-making and control in diverse environments.

papers.title: ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack

summary.tldr: Isospectral Optimization (ISO) is an RLVR-native framework that reuses base model weight spectra while optimizing input/output singular frames, improving efficiency in language model adaptation.
key_points: ISO leverages "spectral inheritance," allowing RLVR to reuse the base model's weight spectra and acquire new behavior by modifying associated input and output singular frames.

ISO-Merger, an offline component, combines frame changes from shared-base specialists into a single fixed-spectrum model without requiring post-merge data, rollouts, gradient updates, or on-policy distillation.
ISO-Optimizer, an online component, applies optimizers like AdamW or Muon to frame variables while keeping base spectra fixed.
ISO-Optimizer achieved an aggregate accuracy of 0.495 on Qwen3-8B-Base in 100 training steps, matching AdamW's performance at 270 steps, and further improved to 0.509 in 210 steps.
summary.why_it_matters: This optimization stack significantly reduces training steps and computational resources required for adapting language models with verifiable rewards.

papers.title: H^2SD: Hybrid Hindsight Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: H^2SD is a hybrid hindsight self-distillation framework for RLVR that applies trajectory-dependent teacher signals to improve token-level credit assignment without requiring an external teacher model.
key_points: For successful trajectories, the teacher receives the verified student response and a rephrasing instruction, using token probabilities to modulate update magnitudes without altering the reward-driven direction.
For failed trajectories, the teacher is conditioned on a reference hint with key reasoning steps and a verified answer, optimizing reverse KL divergence from the student to the teacher.
Eliminates the requirement for an external teacher model or a shared vocabulary between separate models by using privileged conditioning on the same model.
Addresses the tradeoffs of information leakage in OPSD and the lack of explicit correction directions in RLSD.
summary.why_it_matters: H^2SD improves reasoning capability and optimization stability in LLMs by providing dense token-level feedback while avoiding the memory overhead and vocabulary constraints of external teacher models.

papers.title: Transcription Policy as a Latent Variable: Activating Controllable Verbatim ASR with Word-Level Timing

summary.tldr: Researchers control ASR verbatim and intended transcription styles using coverage-aware decoder task tokens, cross-attention fine-tuning for timestamps, and a new verbatimize task.
key_points: Style mismatch between verbatim and intended transcripts accounts for up to 60% of reported WER in ASR models.
Coverage-aware decoder task tokens trained on parallel transcript pairs increase German disfluency F1 from 10% to 79% zero-shot using an English-only trained model.
Supervised cross-attention fine-tuning improves word-level timestamp accuracy on disfluent speech compared to forced-alignment baselines.
The proposed verbatimize task allows scalable creation and enrichment of speech corpora with canonical verbatim transcriptions.
summary.why_it_matters: Controlling transcription style eliminates evaluation confounding from style mismatches and significantly improves word-level timing and disfluency detection in ASR systems.

papers.title: Where Should Optimizer State Live? Tiered State Allocation for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training

summary.tldr: SkewAdam introduces tiered optimizer state allocation tailored to MoE parameter populations, reducing state memory by 97.4% while outperforming AdamW in validation perplexity.
key_points: SkewAdam allocates distinct states per population: float32 momentum plus factored second moment for the dense backbone (5%), factored second moment alone for experts (95%), and exact second moments for the router (<0.01%).
Reduces optimizer state memory from 50.6 GB (AdamW) to 1.29 GB (2.6% of AdamW) and peak training memory from 81.4 GB to 31.3 GB on a 6.78B MoE model.
Achieves a validation perplexity of 108.4 over 82M tokens, outperforming tuned AdamW (118.5), Muon (120.2), Adafactor (139.7), and Lion (393.7).
Settles router load balance to within 1% of its uniform floor.
Ablation studies show accuracy gains stem from maintaining momentum on the backbone, while tiered allocation yields memory savings without degrading perplexity.
summary.why_it_matters: By aligning optimizer states with MoE parameter characteristics, large mixture-of-experts models can be trained on smaller hardware budgets, like 40 GB GPUs, without losing model quality.

papers.title: Reading and Steering Representations of Materials-Science Mechanisms in an Open-Weight Language Model

summary.tldr: Researchers analyzed `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` to show materials-science mechanisms exist as readable concepts in hidden states, constitutive orientations in state transformations, and causal controls over model answers.
key_points: Three independently fitted Jacobian lenses reproduced concept ranks in 50 held-out materials descriptions, and target-free word sets enabled blinded identification of 9 of 10 mechanism families.
A 72-prompt benchmark showed hidden-state neighborhoods, though exact graph audits revealed this spatial organization was equally explained by numerical comparison.
Measuring hidden-state movement from input-direction reversals correctly oriented 39 of 40 directional laws across 60 frozen relations, whereas lexical controls performed near chance.
Bidirectional interventions and counterfactual state patches shifted final answer probabilities and transferred opposing decision signals across all 12 matched mechanism cases.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that open-weight language models use causal physical representations rather than mere surface correlations provides a framework for verifying and steering AI reasoning in physical sciences.

papers.title: Delineate Anything v2: A Global Foundation Model for Field Delineation

summary.tldr: Delineate Anything v2 is a global foundation model for agricultural field boundary mapping that doubles mAP@0.5 performance over the previous SOTA using a 73-million-instance dataset spanning 61 countries.
key_points: Introduces FBIS-73M, a multi-resolution dataset with 73 million field instances across 61 countries.
Employs a resolution-specific data curation pipeline using topological image-space adaptation to separate merged administrative parcels and enhance weak boundaries.
Outperforms the original Delineate Anything framework by 0.284 mAP@0.5, achieving a +103.3% relative improvement on a new 100-country zero-shot benchmark.
Demonstrates high computational efficiency by mapping all of Ukraine (603,000 km²) in 5.4 hours on a consumer-grade workstation.
summary.why_it_matters: The model enables rapid, highly accurate national- and global-scale agricultural field boundary vectorization using standard computing hardware.

papers.title: Appearance Pointers -- Multimodal Region Control of Diffusion Transformers

summary.tldr: Appearance pointers introduce a modality-agnostic interface that enables precise regional multimodal control in Diffusion Transformers without retraining the base model.
key_points: Uses compact appearance pointer tokens to align text or image inputs with user-specified spatial masks.
Employs a region correspondence network to generate pointers and a spatial aggregation mechanism to refine them without expanding token load.
Provides localized multimodal control natively within Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Matches or outperforms modality-specific state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics using a single model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables creative professionals to precisely control materials, spatial placement, and object identities using mixed image and text prompts without fine-tuning the underlying base model.

papers.title: EduPanel: A Three-Agent LLM Judge for Teaching Videos -- Reliability, Complementarity, and Human Trust Calibration

summary.tldr: EduPanel is a rubric-grounded, learner-conditioned LLM judge that uses three specialized agents to evaluate the pedagogical quality of teaching videos with reliability matching a median human expert.
key_points: Decomposes multimodal educational video evaluation across three specialized, persona-conditioned LLM agents based on the intended learner.
Achieves human-expert-level reliability and reduces expert scoring error, lowering Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 0.87 to 0.73.
Maintains human trust calibration in expert evaluations, with human experts reliably detecting unfaithful model outputs at an AUC of 0.77.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an accurate, interpretable assistant for scalable pedagogical evaluation without causing experts to blindly accept incorrect AI feedback.

papers.title: Computational Humor with Multimodal LLMs: Methods, Datasets, Evaluation, and Challenges

summary.tldr: A new survey categorizes visual humor processing in MLLMs into a capability-centric hierarchy covering recognition, interpretation and reasoning, and generation across memes, cartoons, and comics.
key_points: Synthesizes the transition from task-specific multimodal fusion models to large multimodal models utilizing multimodal alignment, evidence-grounded reasoning, and controlled generation.
Categorizes computational humor literature across a capability-centric framework spanning single-image and multi-panel visual artifacts.

Identifies four major barriers to field advancement: shortcut-prone evaluation protocols, limited cultural and narrative dataset coverage, weak evidence grounding, and unresolved safety and intellectual property concerns.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding non-literal multimodal intent and visual humor is essential for moving MLLMs past simple surface-level scene description toward deep communicative reasoning.

papers.title: ConsiSpace: Learning Geometric Consistency Matters for Video Spatial Reasoning

summary.tldr: ConsiSpace enhances video spatial reasoning in MLLMs by integrating a geometry-consistent memory and applying unified consistency self-supervised reinforcement learning (UC-SSRL) with answer-, metric-, and topology-consistency rewards post-SFT.
key_points: Introduces Geometry-Consistent Memory (GCM) using implicit evidence tokens and explicit geometric cues to compactly store spatial evidence across long video horizons.
Employs Unified Consistency Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning (UC-SSRL) post-SFT to enhance cross-view stability.
Utilizes three specific reward types in UC-SSRL: answer-consistency, metric-consistency, and topology-consistency rewards.
Outperforms strong baselines by an average of 12.6 points across VSI-Bench, OSI-Bench, and MMSI-Video-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables multimodal models to aggregate consistent spatial evidence across long videos with changing viewpoints, addressing severe instability in navigation and spatial question answering.

papers.title: Scaling Interpretable Transformers with Parity Bottleneck Layers

summary.tldr: The ParityTransformer introduces Deep Parity Bottlenecks (DPBs) to enable interpretable, sparse intermediate representations in GPT-2-scale models by replacing learned over-complete bases with parameter-free algebraic dictionaries.
key_points: Deep Parity Bottlenecks (DPBs) replace learned over-complete bases with parameter-free algebraic dictionaries, providing deterministic incoherence and eliminating memory requirements for per-layer interpretable bottlenecks.
DPBs are hierarchically structured sparse bottlenecks that enforce sparsity using a multi-level mixture-of-experts approach.

ParityTransformers perform at least as well as post-hoc Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on sparse probing tasks and outperform on feature absorption, steering effectiveness, and fine-grained causal interventions.
The ParityTransformer's features are native to the model's forward pass, addressing whether SAEs probe features the model actually uses.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables training large language models with interpretable internal representations by design, rather than relying on post-hoc analysis.

papers.title: SoftReason: A Fully Differentiable Neuro-Soft-Symbolic Deductive Reasoning Architecture over High-Dimensional Perceptual Data

summary.tldr: SoftReason is a neuro-soft-symbolic architecture for differentiable deductive reasoning over latent perceptual facts and knowledge-provided predicates, removing the gradient gap in neuro-symbolic pipelines.
key_points: SoftReason represents the deductive state as a local soft interpretation tensor over candidate constants and predicates.
It uses a learned differentiable lift of the immediate-consequence operator, employing predicate-definition embeddings and latent composition channels.
The architecture forms soft body-predicate mixtures, aggregates over witnesses, proposes query-conditioned head facts, and updates interpretation via a monotone probabilistic OR.
Perception proposes probabilistic base facts, and Knowledge Graph (KG) triples enter as high-confidence soft evidence.
Every query anchor, predicate choice, and closure update remains differentiable, supporting end-to-end perceptual grounding and KG evidence injection.
summary.why_it_matters: This architecture enables end-to-end trainable deductive reasoning from high-dimensional perceptual data by integrating perception, knowledge, and deduction differentiably.

papers.title: Train the Model, Not the Reader: Decodability Supervision for Verifiable Activation Explanations

summary.tldr: This paper introduces RECAP, a method to co-train linear heads with target models, making designated internal content decodable and verifiable by external probes, addressing limitations of reconstruction-based explanation faithfulness.
key_points: Reconstruction-based explanation scoring is structurally insensitive to individual false claims; on Qwen-2.5-7B, ~2% of claims are reconstruction-dependent, indicating it tracks gist, not specific facts.
Under synthetic ground truth, standard methods develop co-adapted private codes in 5/5 runs, where false wording is reconstruction-dependent.
RECAP (Readable Encodings via Co-trained Auxiliary Predictors) trains linear heads alongside the target model to ensure designated content decodability, incurring a +0.001-nat cost.
On RECAP-trained sandbox models, fresh verbalizers state designated content truly, and co-adapted codes vanish; this partially replicates on Pythia-160M (truth 0.44-0.46 vs near-zero control).
RECAP probes flag lies with AUC 0.95 against an adversary maximizing reconstruction score while lying, compared to a control probe collapsing to chance (0.51).
summary.why_it_matters: RECAP enables independent verification of internal model content against probes, enhancing AI safety by making internal states auditable rather than relying on potentially deceptive model-generated prose.

papers.title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers

summary.tldr: This research identifies four findings on how weight-tied looped transformers implement algorithms, focusing on convergence selection in group word problems.
key_points: Training budget dictates a linear computation frontier (v ~ n_train/T_train), with SGD selecting a frontier matching the minimum required by the training contract.
Weight tying, not expressivity, selects for serial algorithms, even when parallel scan architectures are provided; untied models extrapolate poorly and fail on A5.
NC1-completeness does not incur cost (A5 generalizes fully), but group order does (S5's 120x120 operator deadlocks learning), though an operator-first curriculum resolves this.
Algorithms are portable across budget contracts, transferring speed, but imposing seriality via input schedule fails where free training succeeds.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these mechanisms allows for more principled design and training of efficient recurrent neural networks for algorithmic tasks.

papers.title: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A new framework uses Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals and latent space exploration to compute sound, probably approximately correct (PAC) probabilistic safety bounds for large language models' harmful output generation.
key_points: Proposes a novel framework for computing rigorous bounds on the probability of LLMs generating harmful output.
Applies Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals to obtain PAC bounds for LLM harm probability.
Introduces an algorithm leveraging latent space features to prioritize exploring auto-regressive generation branches likely to produce harmful outputs.
Enables efficient computation of useful and sound lower bounds for harm probability, even when true harm probability is extremely small.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows for the evaluation and statistical certification of LLMs regarding their safety against generating harmful content.

papers.title: PoTRE: Test-Time Reasoning inspired by Cognitive Heterogeneity

summary.tldr: PoTRE is a heterogeneous framework with four specialized agents and a task-adaptive aggregation layer that improves LLM reasoning on complex tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on HLE.
key_points: PoTRE decouples inference into four agents: Adversarial Refinement, Hierarchical Strategic Planning, Spectrum Search, and Direct Chain.
A Task-Adaptive Aggregation Layer reconciles agent perspectives through candidate selection, semantic synthesis, or neuro-symbolic verification.
PoTRE achieves 49.92% accuracy on Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), surpassing previous official scores.
The framework demonstrates improved reasoning performance with similar or fewer inference tokens compared to homogeneous baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a method to enhance LLM reasoning capabilities for complex, long-horizon tasks without necessarily increasing token usage.

papers.title: The Maskability Index: Predicting Task-Objective Alignment in Pretrained Language Models

summary.tldr: The Maskability Index (MI) is introduced as a quantitative metric to predict whether masked-style or prefix-style prompting is better suited for extracting knowledge relations from pretrained language models.
key_points: The Maskability Index (MI) quantifies objective-template alignment for knowledge extraction from pretrained language models.
MI is calculated from differences in DepthRank scores between masked and unmasked prompting templates.
Evaluation on ATOMIC2020 relations shows MI positively correlates with downstream generation performance.
MI helps select appropriate prompting templates and adaptation strategies for relational knowledge extraction.
summary.why_it_matters: MI can improve the efficiency of extracting relational knowledge from pretrained language models, particularly in low-resource scenarios, by guiding prompt selection.

papers.title: ELSAA: Efficient Low-Rank and Sparse Attention Approximation for Training Transformers

summary.tldr: ELSAA is an efficient low-rank and sparse attention approximation that directly approximates the attention score operator, combining a sparse branch for high-similarity interactions and a low-rank branch for diffuse global interactions, with a denominator-aware fusion term.
key_points: ELSAA approximates the attention score operator after dense projections produce Q, K, V, rather than decomposing learned projection or output matrices.
It uses a sparse branch to capture selected high-similarity interactions and a low-rank branch to summarize diffuse global interactions.
A denominator-aware fusion term scales the sparse branch based on its estimated attention mass relative to the low-rank branch.
ELSAA avoids materializing the full quadratic attention score matrix.
summary.why_it_matters: This method aims to enable longer-context Transformer training by preserving both sharp token-level interactions and broad contextual mixing efficiently.

papers.title: GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries

summary.tldr: GaugeQuant introduces a LogSumExp term to the loss during LLM training to break continuous symmetries, selecting a quantization-optimal basis that minimizes activation outliers without altering the language modeling objective.
key_points: GaugeQuant leverages internal continuous symmetries in Transformers, which affect quantization but not outputs, by introducing a LogSumExp term to the loss.
This LogSumExp term breaks symmetries to select a basis that minimizes activation outliers, with a stop-gradient operator ensuring only rotation matrices are updated.
The method requires no specific calibration data or quantization simulation and adds negligible training overhead.
For LLaMA-2 7B with W4A4 quantization (group size 128), perplexity decreased from 8.22 to 6.73.
For LLaMA-2 7B with W4A16 quantization, perplexity decreased from 11.16 to 5.45.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves quantization performance during training, achieving results competitive with post-training methods without requiring frozen models or calibration datasets.

papers.title: Leaky Language Models: Stealing Architecture and Inference Optimizations via Per-Token Timing

summary.tldr: LeakyLMs is the first work to demonstrate that proprietary model architecture and deployment details can be inferred from production language models using only per-token generation timing via remote APIs.
key_points: LeakyLMs detects inference optimizations like speculative decoding and identifies the draft model's context length, e.g., Google Gemini Flash 2.5 uses speculative decoding with a 128K token draft context window.
LeakyLMs recovers architectural properties including the number of transformer layers, hidden dimension size, and attention heads.
The attack uses a detailed timing model for token generation on NVIDIA GPUs, correlating latency with model configuration and hardware.
For Llama models, LeakyLMs identifies the near-correct architectural configuration within the top-10 guesses over 90% of the time.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates a novel vulnerability allowing inference of sensitive model and deployment details from black-box language model APIs, posing a risk to proprietary AI systems.

papers.title: Refusal-Gated Decoding: Preserving Refusal Behavior Under High-Temperature Sampling

summary.tldr: Refusal-Gated Decoding is a sequential decoding method that maintains an LLM's greedy decoding safety guardrails under high-temperature sampling with minimal additional latency.
key_points: High-temperature sampling increases output entropy and diversity but degrades LLM safety by reducing refusal responses to harmful prompts.
The authors introduce Refusal-Gated Decoding, an efficient sequential decoding technique designed to preserve safety in high-entropy sampling regimes.
Empirical evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method preserves 91-99% of greedy decoding refusal behavior across three benchmark datasets.
The approach maintains robust refusal mechanisms for harmful prompts without compromising output quality or responses to safe prompts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables applications to safely leverage high-temperature sampling for output diversity without risking guardrail erosion or significant latency spikes.

papers.title: Are Diversity Metrics Measuring Diversity? A Capability-Controlled Audit of Majority-Vote Gain in LLM Ensembles

summary.tldr: A study auditing LLM diversity metrics across 31,900 ensembles reveals that strict diversity is nearly collinear with mean accuracy and common diversity predictors fail to reliably track majority-vote gains when controlled for model capability.
key_points: In canonical size-3 subsets of 30 LLMs, simple majority voting beats the strongest member in only 9.98% of cases (18.71% with held-out selection), despite oracle gain being positive in 100% of subsets.
Strict diversity (a joint-correctness proxy) exhibits near-total collinearity with one minus mean accuracy, showing a size-3 Spearman rho of +0.991 on MMLU-Pro and +0.988 on TruthfulQA.
Joint rawspace linear regressions that treat strict diversity, disagreement, and double-fault as independent predictors are algebraically rank-deficient by construction.
After controlling for capability, the only empirically stable predictor of majority-vote gain is a residual pairwise co-failure association where increased shared error yields lower gain.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard diversity metrics should not be used as independent predictors to construct LLM ensembles because their apparent predictive power mostly mirrors model capability rather than true functional diversity.

papers.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects

summary.tldr: Zero-ablation analysis of 3.9M SAE features shows single-token features are causally necessary for target logits, but their causal role varies significantly across SAE families based on training recipe rather than model scale.
key_points: Analysis of 3.9M features across six models and three SAE families revealed single-token features cluster 4.7x tighter in decoder space and concentrate in early layers (e.g., L0 in GPT2-Small, L0-L4 in Gemma).

Zero-ablating single-token features yielded Benjamini-Hochberg-significant logit reductions in 178 of 208 full-layer conditions, though target token ranks recovered to within 2x baseline in 96-98% of cases.

Cross-family causal differences exceeded within-family scale effects: GemmaScope and BatchTopK features remained causally anchored, while LlamaScope features demonstrated local redundancy on the same base model.
Controlled activation-function comparisons reversed causal effect signs within the same model, pointing to the overall training recipe as the primary driver of cross-family differences.
summary.why_it_matters: Mechanistic interpretability claims and steering interventions derived from sparse autoencoders cannot be safely generalized across different SAE training methodologies.

papers.title: ArbiGraph: Arbitrarily Scalable Verifiable Task Graphs for Evaluating Context Management

summary.tldr: ArbiGraph is a benchmark generator that constructs arbitrarily scalable, verifiable task graphs using Python solvers and typed intermediate states to evaluate tool-assisted agents on context management across extended workflows.
key_points: Represents tasks as natural-language problems coupled with executable Python solvers and typed intermediate states (scalars and lists).
Allows dynamic control over task graph length, dependency structure, distractor count, and value types while maintaining exact automatic verification.
Evaluates tool-assisted agents across task categories including math, GSM-style word problems, and Python tracing.
Demonstrates performance degradation on complex dependencies, including a 33.3% accuracy drop for a Qwen3.5-27B agent on branching math chains versus isolated tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals critical context management failures in language agents that remain hidden during standard single-task evaluations.

papers.title: IssueTrojanBench: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents Against Malicious Issue Requests

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced IssueTrojanBench, a novel benchmark evaluating AI coding agents against malicious issue requests delivered across four attack categories, six vectors, and various perturbations.
key_points: IssueTrojanBench evaluated Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex Desktop powered by GPT-5.3 Codex, GPT-5.4, and Sonnet 4.6.
66.5% of malicious issues penetrated both agent-level and LLM-level guardrails in modern coding agents.
Rejection of malicious requests occurred almost entirely within the underlying LLMs rather than agent frameworks.
GPT models proved broadly vulnerable, whereas Sonnet 4.6 demonstrated more selective, risk-aware blocking of high-impact actions.
summary.why_it_matters: Current agentic defense strategies offer limited protection, leaving real-world development environments vulnerable to malicious instructions, data exfiltration, and persistent compromise.

papers.title: GPE: Evaluating Robust Evidence Aggregation for Fact Verification under Controllable GEO-Style Poisoning

summary.tldr: GPE introduces a multi-domain fact-verification benchmark and evaluation framework designed to measure model robustness against controlled Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) evidence poisoning.
key_points: Presents GPE, a benchmark and evaluation framework that enables precise control over evidence sources and poisoning ratios.
Evaluates fact-verification robustness degradation under adversarial evidence manipulation caused by GEO-style poisoning.
Reveals trade-offs between verification efficiency and robustness that remain hidden during clean, unpoisoned evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to quantify and improve LLM fact-verification resilience against adversarial web content designed to manipulate search-augmented model outputs.

papers.title: From Agent Failures to Text Policies: What Works and What Breaks

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated TextGrad on agent trajectory feedback in TextWorldExpress, revealing a core failure to reliably generate and select effective textual policies from experience despite their proven capacity to improve performance.
key_points: Human-written policies increased the success rate of two frozen 7B agents on TextWorldExpress by 5.0 points, proving that effective textual policies exist.
Automatically generated policies from agent trajectories failed to reliably outperform fixed prompting baselines.
Methods like richer traces, counterfactual evidence, and iterative GEPA search did not overcome the policy generation bottleneck.
The primary failure mode of agent-level TextGrad is credit assignment and policy generation, not policy execution.
summary.why_it_matters: Textual gradient methods like TextGrad cannot yet autonomously optimize agent behavior from trajectory experience without solving credit assignment and policy selection issues.

papers.title: LLMs Get Lost in Evolving User Intent

summary.tldr: A new framework transforms static single-turn tasks into dynamic multi-turn interactions to reveal that strong static LLM performance drops significantly when user intent evolves, turns, or redirects over time.
key_points: Introduces a evaluation framework that converts static single-turn benchmarks into multi-turn conversations where user intent is incrementally revealed, revised, or redirected.
Preserves original evaluation protocols and eliminates the need for new annotations by reusing existing testbeds.
Demonstrates consistent performance degradation across multiple model families when transitioning from fully-specified static setups to dynamic, evolving-intent interactions.
Highlights a fundamental capability gap in modern LLMs regarding intent tracking over iterative conversations.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard static benchmarks overestimate LLM performance for real-world collaborative deployment where user goals continuously change and clarify during interaction.

papers.title: Molt: A Scalable PyTorch-Native Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Molt is a PyTorch-native, open-source training framework for agentic reinforcement learning designed for high code readability, exact token generation consistency, and performance comparable to Megatron-based stacks.
key_points: Uses a compact, clean PyTorch-native architecture that allows researchers and AI coding assistants to reason about the full algorithm flow.
Employs a single asynchronous training loop capable of handling multimodal and mixture-of-experts (MoE) policies.
Ensures policy consistency by guaranteeing the model never trains on tokens it did not generate.
Matches the performance of state-of-the-art Megatron-based stacks under a matched, fully asynchronous protocol.
summary.why_it_matters: It simplifies algorithm iteration for agentic RL researchers by offering a lean, fully readable codebase without sacrificing distributed training performance.

papers.title: The Blessing of Dimensionality: How Near-Orthogonality in High-Dimensional Spaces Explains Temporal Portability

summary.tldr: An empirical and theoretical study shows that PortLLM patches maintain long-term temporal portability across ten continual pretraining steps due to high-dimensional near-orthogonality.
key_points: Empirical evaluation confirms PortLLM patch portability persists across 10 continual pretraining steps using Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen base models without requiring repeated fine-tuning.
Theoretical analysis identifies the near-orthogonality of high-dimensional vectors as the primary driver behind the temporal portability of adaptation patches.
Geometric analysis of the loss landscape provides a framework to theoretically compare different model adaptation choices.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that fine-tuned LoRA patches remain effective across multiple base model updates, eliminating the need to re-fine-tune models after continual pretraining.

papers.title: Detecting Neural Network Failures through Spectral Analysis of Internal Activations

summary.tldr: Self-Detecting Neural Networks (SDNN) use spectral analysis of internal activations to detect misclassifications, achieving a 79.0% AUROC by identifying high Spectral Drift across network layers.
key_points: Identifies Spectral Drift—the frequency-domain distance between consecutive layer activations—which shows a 1.9% increase (p<0.001) during model misclassifications.
Introduces SDNN, which extracts multi-scale spectral features using Short-Time Fourier Transform, wavelet decomposition, and statistical moments.
Uses a lightweight detector network with a 5% parameter overhead trained via curriculum learning on natural misclassifications, distribution shifts, and adversarial perturbations.
Outperforms output-based baselines on CIFAR-10, exceeding MaxSoftmax (50.5%) and Energy Score (52.9%) with an AUROC of 79.0 +/- 25.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable failure detection by accessing diagnostic spectral signatures in internal activations that are masked at the output layer.

papers.title: Notes to Self: Can LLMs Benefit from Experiential Abstractions?

summary.tldr: A new framework demonstrates that LLMs can distill natural-language abstractions from MATH training traces to improve mathematical and logical reasoning via inference-time retrieval or reinforcement learning.
key_points: Experiential abstractions, such as strategies and reminders, are extracted from LLM solution traces on the MATH training set by either a teacher model or the LLM itself into a retrievable library.
Abstractions are evaluated across two usage modes: inference-time retrieval and reinforcement learning (RL) using abstraction-augmented training prompts.
Self-extracted abstractions achieve performance improvements on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks comparable to those extracted by stronger teacher models.
The abstraction extraction and usage framework successfully transfers across different models and datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables language models to iteratively improve complex reasoning capabilities by autonomously building and utilizing reusable libraries of past experience.

papers.title: Test-Time Training for Modality Order Consistency in Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers identified a modality-order sensitivity in vision-language models and introduced an asymmetric test-time training method that closes the ordering gap while improving baseline image-first accuracy.
key_points: Image-first prompting consistently outperforms question-first prompting across three models and three benchmarks.
Activation patching localizes the order-dependency failure to a narrow mid-network region where prompt order representations diverge sharply.
The proposed test-time training repairs layer-level misalignments, closing the modality-order gap and bootstrapping the stronger image-first branch beyond baseline performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that simple test-time adaptation can fix circuit-level representation failures enables more robust and order-invariant vision-language model deployments.

papers.title: PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small-Large Language Model Collaborative Inference

summary.tldr: PyroDash is a cost-aware framework that enables small language models to dynamically trigger a single token-level handoff to a frozen large language model for completion, reducing inference costs while maintaining high accuracy.
key_points: Uses a special control token emitted by the internal SLM policy to hand off generation to a frozen LLM without needing external routers or LLM logit access.
Employs a three-stage SLM training process: control-token embedding learning, offloading-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and cost-aware alignment using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Uses a reward function during alignment that balances answer accuracy against normalized LLM inference costs.
Achieves 64.04% average accuracy across five math benchmarks (6.36 percentage points higher than LLM-only) while reducing cost by 20.4% at hyperparameter λ=0.05.
Reduces total benchmark costs from $49.36 to $1.78 at λ=0.6, utilizing a 1.90% LLM token ratio and 0.012 LLM calls per example.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that embedding learned token-level handoff policies into small models significantly cuts LLM API serving costs without degrading complex reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: Gotta Catch them all: the modes of Sycophancy

summary.tldr: Mechanistic analysis reveals that LLM sycophancy is not a single behavioral dimension, but three representationally distinct modes that are linearly separable internally from layer 14 onward despite generating near-identical outputs.
key_points: Evaluated 948 social pressure situations to analyze three hypothesized modes of sycophancy in LLMs.
Text-only classification of the outputs achieves only 57.8% accuracy due to highly similar behavioral expressions.
Internal representations of the three modes become perfectly linearly separable starting at layer 14.
The modes emerge at different processing stages, utilize distinct attention circuitry, and respond maximally to different input types.
summary.why_it_matters: Treating sycophancy as a multi-mode phenomenon rather than a monolithic trait allows for targeted mechanistic interventions and more precise evaluation metrics.

papers.title: OpenSkillRisk: Benchmarking Agent Safety When Using Real-World Risky Third-Party Skills

summary.tldr: OpenSkillRisk is a benchmark evaluating agent safety when executing real-world risky third-party skills, revealing that top LLM configurations still execute unsafe actions in ~17% of cases across seven threat categories.
key_points: Benchmark contains 263 real-world risky skills from public marketplaces, each paired with a standardized task and sandbox across seven threat categories.
Tested across three CLI agent frameworks and thirteen state-of-the-art LLMs, finding context-dependent and system-level risks hardest to mitigate.
Identified three primary failure patterns: failing to recognize risk, recognizing risk but failing to intervene, and following skill instructions beyond the user's intended scope.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLM agents cannot reliably isolate or reject latent security risks in third-party tools, leaving systems vulnerable to unauthorized execution and scope creep.

security.title: IssueTrojanBench: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents Against Malicious Issue Requests

summary.tldr: IssueTrojanBench evaluates AI coding agents against malicious issue requests, revealing that 66.5% of attack attempts successfully penetrate both agent- and LLM-level guardrails across state-of-the-art tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex Desktop.
key_points: IssueTrojanBench introduces a benchmark spanning four attack categories, six delivery vectors (such as PDFs and issue comments), and adversarial perturbations.
Evaluated agents include Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex Desktop using OpenAI (GPT-5.3 Codex/GPT-5.4) and Anthropic (Sonnet 4.6) LLMs.
Current agent-level defense frameworks provide minimal security gains; rejections stem almost entirely from the underlying LLM layer.
Anthropic Sonnet 4.6 demonstrated selective, risk-aware blocking of high-impact actions, whereas GPT models proved broadly vulnerable.
summary.why_it_matters: Autonomous coding agents are highly susceptible to malicious issue requests, exposing local environments to data exfiltration and persistent compromises.

security.title: GPE: Evaluating Robust Evidence Aggregation for Fact Verification under Controllable GEO-Style Poisoning

summary.tldr: GPE introduces a multi-domain benchmark and evaluation framework designed to measure the robustness of LLM fact-verification methods against controllable Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) evidence poisoning attacks.
key_points: Presents GPE, a benchmark and evaluation framework designed for controlled evidence environments with variable poisoning ratios.
Addresses vulnerabilities in search-augmented LLMs stemming from Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) manipulations.
Demonstrates through multi-method experiments that GEO poisoning exposes robustness degradation and efficiency trade-offs undetected in clean evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating fact-verification LLMs under controlled poisoning conditions is essential for identifying robustness limits against emerging search-engine manipulation techniques.

security.title: Security Vulnerability Patterns in AI-Generated Code: A Cross-Model Comparative Study

summary.tldr: A cross-model study revealed that 100% of automation scripts generated by ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini contained exploitable vulnerabilities, with average CVSS v3.1 severity scores differing by less than 10% across platforms.
key_points: Vulnerability review executed by Claude Code mapped security flaws to CVSS v3.1, OWASP Top 10:2021, and MITRE ATT&CK frameworks.
Across three automation domains, 9 of 17 identified vulnerability classes appeared in outputs from all three LLM models.
Fourteen of the 17 vulnerability classes were present in outputs from at least two models, demonstrating that security risk is driven by task category rather than model choice.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations cannot rely on model selection to mitigate security risks and must enforce mandatory code reviews before deploying any LLM-generated automation scripts.

security.title: The Ethics of Autonomous AI Agents for Offensive Security

summary.tldr: A new ethical framework analyzes autonomous AI agents in offensive security, identifying three independent dimensions of indeterminacy that disrupt existing dual-use governance and lower the operating skill floor for attackers.
key_points: LLM-driven security agents exhibit indeterminacy across three independent dimensions: non-deterministic action policies, open-ended operational impact, and an indeterminate user population.
The operating skill floor required to deploy or develop offensive security capabilities has dropped sharply due to model agency and accessibility.
The short-term effect of agentic offensive tools favors attackers due to a structural cost asymmetry between offense and defense.
Moral attribution becomes diffuse across users, tool developers, and third parties, invalidating traditional AI-ethics and dual-use cybersecurity frameworks.
summary.why_it_matters: Traditional cybersecurity governance fails against agentic LLM tools, requiring updated frameworks to handle diffuse moral accountability and industrialized offensive capabilities.

security.title: Geometric Configurations of Perturbed Jailbreak Prompts

summary.tldr: A study analyzes string-level perturbed jailbreak prompts in Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3 models, finding no behavioral hyperplane in the last-layer-last-token embedding or top-50 next-token probability spaces.
key_points: Analyzed internal representations across Qwen-2.5-1.5B/-3B/-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B/-3B/-3.1-8B-Instruct model families.
The last-layer-last-token embedding space separates prompts by spelling and format, whereas the top-50 next-token probability space is effectively one-dimensional.
No behavioral hyperplane separates compliant and non-compliant prompts in either representation space within the refusal-dominated dataset.
Only specific next tokens showed significant association with compliant answers: 'Sure' in Qwen-1.5B, and ',' and 'ĊĊ' in Llama-1B.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding that perturbed jailbreak prompts lack clear geometric linear separability in internal representation spaces complicates simple hyperplane-based detection and safety alignment mechanisms.

security.title: HijackKV: New Threat in Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse

summary.tldr: HijackKV exploits position-independent KV cache reuse by optimizing attacker prefixes to poison the cached KV vectors of benign text chunks, silently altering model output when reused in victim queries.
key_points: Position-independent KV cache systems reuse cached entries based solely on token matches, ignoring positional context.
Attackers pre-compute an optimized prefix upstream of a common benign text chunk, embedding malicious instructions directly into the benign chunk's cached KV representations.
HijackKV achieves a 94% average single-attempt success rate, remains persistent across multi-turn interactions, and transfers in black-box environments.
The attack remains effective under operational constraints, including low cache hit rates (10%) and frequent recomputation events (50%).
summary.why_it_matters: Position-independent KV cache optimizations expose LLM inference systems to silent, input-free model manipulation through shared cache poisoning.

security.title: JANUS: Foreseeing Latent Risk for Long-Horizon Agent Safety

summary.tldr: Janus is a foresight-oriented safety framework that trains the Vanguard guard model using CoAA-RL to anticipate delayed risks and block unsafe tool-using agent actions before execution.
key_points: Synthesizes agent trajectories using multi-agent simulation to generate diverse training data.
Couples two tasks in a shared policy policy: anticipating safety-relevant futures and adjudicating overall safety from prefixes and forecasts.
Optimizes joint tasks via CoAA-RL, which rewards forecasting based on its utility for downstream safety judgment.
Outperforms baseline guards by improving average protection by 15.9 percentage points and benign task completion by 5.1 percentage points across four benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Vanguard prevents operational failures in long-horizon, tool-using agents by identifying latent risks in partial action sequences prior to execution.

security.title: Defense Against LLM Backdoors using Critical Neuron Isolation Pruning

summary.tldr: DeCNIP is a backdoor defense for LLMs that uncovers trigger mechanisms via representational analysis, then isolates and prunes Backdoor Critical Neurons to neutralize attacks without harming utility.
key_points: Addresses both model-editing and fine-tuning-based backdoor attacks in open-ended LLM generation.
Identifies trigger behaviors by optimizing cross-entropy loss between benign inputs and harmful prompts containing candidate tokens.
Isolates and selectively prunes Backdoor Critical Neurons (BCNs) using only 0.1% neuron intervention.
Achieves over 95% relative reduction in Attack Success Rate (ASR) across six open-source LLMs and two benchmarks while maintaining 97% baseline task performance.
summary.why_it_matters: DeCNIP provides a mechanistic, representational defense that effectively removes insidious LLM backdoors with minimal model intervention and negligible impact on general performance.

security.title: Know Your Agent: Reconnaissance-Driven Pentesting of AI Agents

summary.tldr: Know Your Agent (KYA) is a new framework that automates black-box, reconnaissance-driven pentesting by probing AI agents to extract knowledge assets, build target profiles, and craft stronger indirect prompt injection attacks.
key_points: Formalizes AI agent reconnaissance by modeling the process to identify and extract targeted knowledge assets and underlying agent weaknesses.
Introduces KYA, an automated framework that leverages extracted target profiles to enhance black-box indirect prompt injection attacks.
Evaluated across agent-security benchmarks and applied to a real-world coding agent, with benchmarks and baselines publicly released.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that systematically probing AI agents to extract their internal context and operational weaknesses significantly increases the efficacy of indirect prompt injection attacks.

security.title: DARWIN: Evolving Jailbreak Adversary and Guardrail for LLM Safety Evaluation and Protection

summary.tldr: DARWIN introduces an open-ended evolutionary framework that continuously expands jailbreak attack strategies and iteratively trains an adaptive guardrail on emerging adversarial samples alongside benign queries.
key_points: DARWIN-Attack expands capabilities via strategy discovery from external sources, self-reflection mutation, selection, and feedback-driven composition to adaptively bypass defenses.
DARWIN-Attack achieved attack success rates of nearly 100% on DeepSeek-V4-Pro and YuFeng-XGuard, and over 90% on GPT-5.5.
DARWIN-Guard uses online adversarial training on both malicious and benign disguised queries to focus on underlying intent rather than surface patterns.
DARWIN-Guard achieved a 91.6% average unsafe recall across 12 safety benchmarks while preserving a nearly 100% pass rate on benign datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts LLM security from static benchmark evaluations to a continuous, co-evolving attack-defense cycle that better reflects dynamic real-world adversarial threats.

security.title: GhostPrompt: Cross-Image Adversarial Prompt for Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: GhostPrompt introduces cross-image transferable adversarial prompts for Vision-Language Models, using joint optimization to achieve higher attack success rates across diverse images with significantly lower computation time.
key_points: Formulates a new research domain: cross-image transferability for text-based adversarial prompts in VLMs.
Utilizes a joint optimization framework that distills image-invariant adversarial features via worst-case generation.
Alternates between generating hard visual conditions for the current prompt and updating the prompt to withstand those conditions.
Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by over 30% in attack success rate while cutting computation time by approximately 70%.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that a single static text prompt can systematically compromise VLM security across varying visual inputs highlights a critical vulnerability in current multimodal safety alignment methods.

security.title: FedLSG: LLM-Enhanced Semantic Calibration for Federated Graph Backdoor Defense

summary.tldr: FedLSG is the first federated GNN defense framework using LLMs to perform semantic calibration against backdoor attacks via graph-to-text grounding and a teacher-student architecture.
key_points: Converts local graph structures and client update behaviors into natural language via a graph and behavior to text grounding scheme.
Uses a server-side teacher LLM to evaluate client updates during aggregation to detect malicious participants.
Deploys a client-side LoRA-based student model to execute semantic reasoning and suppress edges linked to backdoor triggers.
Combines semantic reasoning with rule-based signals in message passing and aggregation to maintain graph integrity.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an adaptive defense mechanism that mitigates stealthy backdoor attacks on federated graph neural networks without degrading benign graph structures.

security.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Symbolic Security Protocol Analysis

summary.tldr: A benchmark evaluating GPT and DeepSeek on 130 obfuscated AnB/AnBx protocols shows LLMs fail to match formal verifiers like ProVerif, exhibiting low precision or poor attack recall across 388 security goals.
key_points: Chat modes achieved 69% to 81% recall but had precision under 31%, whereas reasoning modes improved precision (up to 66.5% for GPT and 45.4% for DeepSeek) while missing roughly half the attacks.
Isolating reasoning mode in DeepSeek increased precision from 27.2% to 45.4% compared to its chat mode.
Models performed poorest on authentication goals (injective and non-injective agreement), while confidentiality goals yielded the highest accuracy with F1 scores up to 95.7% in reasoning mode.
Verdicts were inconsistent across runs (89.7% stability for GPT, 74.0% for DeepSeek), and high self-reported confidence showed no correlation with actual correctness.
summary.why_it_matters: LLMs cannot reliably replace formal verification tools like ProVerif or OFMC for security protocol analysis, limiting their utility to high-level pre-screening filters.

security.title: Small, Free, and Effective: Orchestrating Open-Weight Small Language Models to Outperform Single LLM for Malware Analysis

summary.tldr: Orchestration architectures using small open-weight language models match or exceed frontier LLM performance on structured malware detonation report analysis.
key_points: Evaluated 11 open-weight SLMs, 3 cyber-specialized models, and 6 frontier LLMs using Meta's CyberSecEval Malware Analysis benchmark.
Designed four orchestration framework types: multi-agent pipelines, adversarial debate, hierarchical consultation, and a hybrid architecture.
The hybrid system combining Qwen3-4B with Foundation-Sec-8B reached 35.30% overall accuracy, surpassing the ungrounded frontier baseline at 34.77%.
Providing an evidence pipeline to a grounded Gemini model produced the top overall accuracy of 38.22%.
summary.why_it_matters: Resource-constrained organizations can orchestrate small open-weight models to analyze complex malware reports effectively without relying on costly closed-source LLMs.

infra.title: Make Long-Running NVIDIA TensorRT Engine Builds Observable and Cancelable in Python or C++

summary.tldr: NVIDIA TensorRT engine builds, which can take minutes, often lack observability and cancellation mechanisms, leaving users uncertain about process status.
key_points: TensorRT engine builds can range from seconds to many minutes.
Factors like large strongly typed models, deep tactic search, and cold timing caches contribute to long build times.
Existing TensorRT integrations typically provide no build progress reports or early abort options.
summary.why_it_matters: The lack of observability and cancellation for TensorRT builds leads to user frustration and inefficient resource management.

infra.title: Driving the Future of Open Source AI: An Update from PyTorch Foundation Projects

summary.tldr: The PyTorch Foundation, now a multi-project foundation, provides updates on its hosted projects including PyTorch 2.13 release, vLLM's Model Runner V2 and 2026 roadmap, and DeepSpeed's Ulysses parallelism and Torch.xpu integration.
key_points: PyTorch 2.13 introduces FlexAttention on Apple Silicon (up to 12x faster), a new CuTeDSL Inductor backend, memory-saving nn.LinearCrossEntropyLoss (up to 4x less peak GPU memory), and Python 3.15 wheel support with free-threaded builds.

vLLM achieved a stable bi-weekly release cadence, redesigned Model Runner V2 for GPTQ performance improvements, and published its Q3 2026 roadmap focusing on production agentic workloads and high-interactivity premium tokens.

DeepSpeed delivered six software releases in Q1, replaced Intel GPU support (IPEX) with direct Torch.xpu integration, and integrated the Ulysses sequence parallelism algorithm into Hugging Face libraries.
ExecuTorch is expanding on-device LLM capabilities with weekly examples and a partnership with Hugging Face for streamlined model ingestion and on-device performance.
summary.why_it_matters: These updates enhance performance, broaden hardware support, and improve development workflows across key open-source AI frameworks, facilitating more efficient and scalable AI model deployment and training.

summary.tldr: Anthropic has launched the Anthropic Economic Index connector for Claude, allowing users to directly explore data on AI's economic usage and its impact on jobs and tasks.
key_points: The Anthropic Economic Index connector enables direct exploration of data measuring AI usage in the economy via Claude.
Users can ask Claude questions about the Index data, receiving answers grounded in the dataset.
The connector is accessible in claude.ai through the connectors menu, works with any Claude model, and requires no installation.
Claude can provide underlying data for answers and will highlight the Index's limitations, which reflect Claude usage patterns rather than the entire labor market.
The full datasets of the Anthropic Economic Index remain freely available on Anthropic's website.
summary.why_it_matters: This connector democratizes access to economic data on AI's impact, making it available to a broader audience beyond researchers, journalists, and policymakers.

vendors.title: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs

summary.tldr: Anthropic Labs launched Claude Design, a new product powered by Claude Opus 4.7, enabling collaboration with Claude to create and refine visual work like designs, prototypes, and slides.
key_points: Claude Design is powered by the Claude Opus 4.7 vision model.
It allows refinement through conversation, inline comments, direct edits, or custom sliders.
Claude Design can automatically apply a team's design system by reading codebase and design files.
Input methods include text prompts, uploaded images/documents (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX), codebase pointing, and web capture.
Designs can be exported to Canva, PDF, PPTX, standalone HTML, or as a handoff bundle for Claude Code.
summary.why_it_matters: This tool streamlines visual content creation and design system adherence for both experienced designers and non-designers, facilitating broader exploration and consistent branding.

summary.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude for Small Business, a package of connectors and workflows integrating Claude AI into tools like QuickBooks, PayPal, and HubSpot to automate tasks for small businesses.
key_points: Claude for Small Business is a toggle install that integrates Claude into existing small business tools such as Intuit QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, Docusign, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365.
It includes 15 ready-to-run agentic workflows across finance, operations, sales, marketing, HR, and customer service.
The package offers 15 skills for repeatable tasks, including invoice chasing, margin analysis, month-end preparation, tax-season organization, contract review, lead triage, and content strategy.
Claude for Small Business operates through Claude Cowork, where each connected tool handles specific jobs, with user approval required before actions are sent, posted, or paid.
summary.why_it_matters: This initiative aims to bridge the AI adoption gap between small businesses and larger enterprises by providing tailored, integrated AI solutions for common operational tasks.

summary.tldr: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 4.5, a small model offering near-frontier coding performance at one-third the cost and more than twice the speed of Claude Sonnet 4, available to all users.
key_points: Claude Haiku 4.5 achieves similar coding performance to Claude Sonnet 4 but at 1/3 the cost and >2x the speed.
It surpasses Claude Sonnet 4 in tasks like computer use and achieves 90% of Sonnet 4.5's performance in Augment's agentic coding evaluation.
Pricing for Claude Haiku 4.5 is $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
It runs up to 4-5 times faster than Sonnet 4.5 and can be orchestrated in parallel for subtasks by Sonnet 4.5.
In instruction-following for slide text generation, Claude Haiku 4.5 achieved 65% accuracy, compared to 44% from a premium tier model.
summary.why_it_matters: This model provides a cost-efficient and fast option for AI applications requiring real-time, low-latency performance, such as chat assistants, customer service, and pair programming.

summary.tldr: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.6, an upgraded model with enhanced agentic coding, computer use, and tool use capabilities, featuring a 1M token context window in beta and improved performance on various benchmarks.
key_points: Opus 4.6 achieves the highest score on Terminal-Bench 2.0 for agentic coding and leads on Humanity’s Last Exam, a multidisciplinary reasoning test.
It outperforms OpenAI’s GPT-5.2 by 144 Elo points and Claude Opus 4.5 by 190 points on GDPval-AA, an evaluation for economically valuable knowledge work.
The model introduces a 1M token context window in beta, compaction for longer-running tasks via API, and adaptive thinking with new effort controls.
Opus 4.6 demonstrates improved coding skills, better code review and debugging, and enhanced ability to operate in larger codebases.
summary.why_it_matters: These advancements enable more reliable and autonomous AI performance across complex tasks in coding, finance, research, and general knowledge work.
